rows.grounds: measure of what remains of dharma
that of which a portion remains

items.question: How much of dharma remains as the residual portion?
premises: Dharma can be diminished
A residual portion can remain
That remainder is only a quarter
items.inference: Only a quarter of dharma remains as the remainder.
items.plain_english: Only a quarter of dharma remains; that is the remainder.

rows.grounds: action of being severed or elided

items.question: What grammatical formation explains the term lopa in this context?
premises: Lopa means being cut off
The term is formed in an action context
The suffix ghañ is used in that formation
items.inference: Lopa is derived from being cut off with the ghañ suffix in that action.
items.plain_english: Because something is cut off, it is called lopa; in that action the suffix ghañ is used.

items.question: Which funerary and ancestral rites must be performed according to scripture?
premises: Death rites are required observances
Ancestor śrāddha is a required observance
These rites must follow scriptural approval
items.inference: One should perform the death rite and ancestor śrāddha as approved by scripture.
items.plain_english: One should perform the death rite and the ancestral śrāddha in the manner approved by scripture.

rows.grounds: wearing new garments and similar acts

items.question: What additional domestic and personal rites should be duly observed?
premises: Journey rites are observances
House-entering rites are observances
Wearing new garments and similar acts are observances
items.inference: One should also observe rites for journeys, house-entering, and wearing new garments.
items.plain_english: One should also observe the rites for a journey, entering a house, and wearing new garments and the like.

rows.grounds: consecration at the start of building a house

items.question: Which consecration and installation rites are included among required observances?
premises: Beginning a house requires consecration
Deities require ritual installation
These acts belong to the same ritual list
items.inference: The consecration of a house-beginning and the installation of deities should likewise be performed.
items.plain_english: Likewise, one should perform the consecration at the beginning of a house and the installation of deities.

rows.grounds: periodic rites by season, month, and year

items.question: What categories of periodic and obligatory rites must be included in observance?
premises: Rites occur by season, month, and year
Some rites are daily obligations
Some rites are occasional obligations
items.inference: Seasonal, monthly, yearly, daily, and occasional rites are all included.
items.plain_english: Whatever rites are seasonal, monthly, yearly, daily, or occasional must be included.

items.question: By what prescribed method should a person accomplish all these rites?
premises: The speaker has declared a method
All the listed rites must be accomplished
A person is responsible for performing them
items.inference: A person should accomplish all those rites by the method declared by me.
items.plain_english: A person should accomplish all of that by the method I have declared.

items.question: What degraded rebirth awaits one deprived of all ritual observances?
premises: A person can be deprived of all rites
Ritual deprivation has severe consequences
The consequence is a degraded rebirth
items.inference: One deprived of all rites would become a worm in excrement.
items.plain_english: Deprived of all rites, he would become a worm in excrement.

items.question: Under what condition does a performed action yield the opposite result?
premises: Actions are performed with expected outcomes
Certain conditions can reverse outcomes
A reversed action produces the opposite result
items.inference: When an action is done under such a condition, it turns to the opposite result.
items.plain_english: When any action is performed, it may turn out to have the opposite result.

rows.grounds: verse marker in the source text

items.question: What inner defects cause ritual actions to produce contrary outcomes?
premises: Faith affects ritual efficacy
Trust affects ritual efficacy
Absence of these defects reverses the intended result
items.inference: Lack of faith and absence of trust cause actions to turn contrary.
items.plain_english: This happens through lack of faith and absence of trust.

items.question: What consequences follow for a person whose worship angers the deity?
premises: Improper worship can anger a deity
Divine anger brings obstacles
These obstacles can occur repeatedly
items.inference: For such a person the deity is angered and obstacles arise at every step.
items.plain_english: The deity is angered with him, and obstacles confront him at every step.

items.question: What moral status attaches to performing rites by unauthorized paths?
premises: Rites have a prescribed path
One may perform rites by other paths
Using unauthorized paths is a grave transgression
items.inference: Whoever performs a rite by other paths becomes a great sinner.
items.plain_english: Whoever performs a rite by other paths becomes a great sinner.

items.question: What postmortem punishment and duration await one who uses unauthorized ritual paths?
premises: Grave ritual transgression incurs punishment
The punishment is a terrible hell
The duration lasts as long as moon and sun endure
items.inference: He goes to a terrible hell for as long as the moon and sun exist.
items.plain_english: He goes to a terrible hell for as long as the moon and sun endure.

rows.grounds: restricts his status to outward form
one who bears the sacred thread outwardly

items.question: What is the true status of one who bears the sacred thread without proper conduct?
premises: Bearing the thread can be merely outward
Proper conduct determines true status
Failure in conduct brings extreme degradation
items.inference: Such a person is merely a thread-bearer and is even lower than an outcaste.
items.plain_english: He is merely a bearer of the thread, and is even lower than an outcaste.

rows.grounds: sin arising from visiting a prostitute

items.question: What recurring sin accrues daily to the person of degraded ritual status?
premises: Certain acts generate sin
Visiting a prostitute is such an act
For this person the sin recurs daily
items.inference: That man incurs the sin born of approaching a prostitute day by day.
items.plain_english: Day after day, that man incurs the sin born of going to a prostitute.

rows.grounds: offerings are treated as foul matter

items.question: Why do the ancestors refuse to accept offerings from such a person?
premises: Ancestors receive ritual offerings
The person's offerings are ritually tainted
Tainted offerings are rejected as foul
items.inference: Even the ancestors do not partake because his offerings are like impurity and pus.
items.plain_english: Even the ancestors do not partake of his offerings, because they are like impurity and pus.

items.question: In which ritual domains does such a person lack eligibility to participate?
premises: Ritual participation requires eligibility
Divine, ancestral, and family rites are distinct domains
This person lacks qualification in them
items.inference: He has no eligibility in rites to gods, rites to ancestors, or family customs.
items.plain_english: He has no eligibility in rites to the gods, rites to the ancestors, or family customs.

rows.grounds: the intended sense of the statement

items.question: What is the intended meaning of declaring such a person ritually unqualified?
premises: Ritual eligibility depends on proper consecration
The person lacks that consecration
The statement means he is devoid of refinement
items.inference: The meaning is that he would be devoid of proper consecratory refinement.
items.plain_english: The meaning is that he would be devoid of proper consecration.

items.question: What outcomes result from rites performed without proper qualification in this life and beyond?
premises: Rites are performed for fruit in this world and the next
Improper rites fail to yield that fruit
They still involve bodily hardship and loss of wealth
items.inference: There is no fruit here or hereafter, only bodily torment and loss of wealth.
items.plain_english: There is no fruit here or hereafter, only bodily torment and loss of wealth.

items.question: What fate befalls the performer when an ancestral śrāddha proves fruitless?
premises: A śrāddha can be fruitless
Fruitless rites bring adverse consequences
The performer bears that consequence with the ancestors
items.inference: That śrāddha is fruitless and he would go to hell together with the ancestors.
uncertainties: The instrumental pitṛbhiḥ may indicate accompaniment or agency; accompaniment is preferred here.
items.plain_english: That śrāddha is fruitless, and he would go to hell along with the ancestors.

rows.grounds: teaching or path belonging to Śiva
injunction to take refuge in it

items.question: Which doctrinal path should a mortal deliberately adopt to avoid these faults?
premises: Previous verses warn against improper paths
A correct path must be chosen
The Śaiva teaching is prescribed as that path
items.inference: Therefore a mortal should diligently resort to the Śaiva teaching.
items.plain_english: Therefore a mortal should diligently take refuge in the teaching of Śiva.

items.question: What value remains in actions performed outside the way of Śiva?
premises: Actions may be performed outside Śiva's way
Ritual value depends on proper grounding
Actions lacking that grounding lack purpose
items.inference: All action done apart from Śiva's way is meaningless, O goddess.
items.plain_english: O goddess, every action performed apart from the way of Śiva is meaningless.

rows.grounds: one lacking conduct aligned with Śiva

items.question: Can one devoid of Śaiva conduct obtain release from hellish punishment?
premises: Hellish punishment requires release
Śaiva conduct is necessary for release
One may be devoid of Śaiva conduct
items.inference: For one devoid of Śaiva conduct there is indeed no release from hell.
items.plain_english: For one devoid of Śaiva conduct, there is indeed no release from hell.

items.question: What identity is affirmed between the true practice and the goddess's own practice?
premises: A true practice is being identified
The goddess is addressed directly
That practice is equated with her own practice
items.inference: The practice in question is indeed your own practice, O great goddess.
items.plain_english: O great goddess, that practice is indeed your own practice.
